newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity Investments revises code of ethics.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity Investments revises code of ethics.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said it has revised its code of ethics covering personal investing by employees and will release a summary to shareholders of its mutual funds.

Effective in January, employees will be prohibited from short-selling any individual security except for hedging purposes. Prior to the change, the short-selling prohibition applied only to those securities held in Fidelity funds.
The code also includes language discouraging "excessive" selling, which provides further support for Fidelity's existing provisions against short-term trading, Fidelity said.

Also included is a reduction in the time in which employees must acknowledge they have read and understand the code and disclosed their personal holdings. New employees will have one week, rather than 60 days, to submit their acknowledgement. For annual code revisions, the deadline will be one month rather than two months.

"Annually, we review our code and update it and it's always typically this time of year," Fidelity spokeswoman Anne Crowley told Reuters. "This is the first time we've released a summary of the code to shareholders."
Fidelity will provide a copy of the code to shareholders on request and it is also available on Fidelity's web page (http://www.fidelity.com).

The current code also bans investment professionals and senior executives from taking profits on trades of securities held for less than 60 days. They must seek pre-approval for all trades, Fidelity said.
In addition, a portfolio manager may not personally buy or sell a security within seven calendar days before or after his or her fund buys or sells the same security.
